title: The Simulation Argument
summary: Nick Bostrom argued that at least one of three things is true: almost no civilisations like ours reach a stage where they can run detailed simulations of minds; almost none that could are interested in running them; or we are almost certainly living in a simulation ourselves. If simulated worlds are possible and cheap, simulated minds would vastly outnumber real ones, so a mind like yours would be more likely to be one of them.
citations: Nick Bostrom, "Are You Living in a Computer Simulation?" Philosophical Quarterly 53, no. 211 (2003): 243–255: https://www.simulation-argument.com/
reading: David J. Chalmers, Reality+: Virtual Worlds and the Problems of Philosophy (W. W. Norton, 2022)
